Reviewer: coverage_middle. Disposition: **CONDITIONAL PASS at the local literary/source-review role**, subject only to RC-M01's two exact wording edits and the corresponding derivative register row. This does not accept repository currentness, complete R09, convergence, release, models or publication. I read the entire argument, not just its evidence directory: lines 1–90, 91–180 and 181–269. I also read the complete human and machine source/debt receipts, complete authoring-input manifest, complete handoff manifest, and all 22 claim, 24 route and 14 witness-responsibility rows. These are not a new fourteen-novel primary reading. Mechanical replay is separately identified below.

## 1. The affirmative argument survives review

The thesis has a substantive object: attachment creates reasons to answer another person, while the attached person remains a separate chooser of ends. This is more than an accumulation of consent warnings. The manuscript explains why particular people keep acting, why their help is sometimes valuable, and how the same relation creates temptations to exceed its standing. Its distinctions between desire, relationship category, knowledge, standing and capacity give the longitudinal comparison useful terms without presenting those terms as a completed ethics spoken by the novels.

The early couple material is particularly important. Created access and practiced presentation do not make all later intimacy counterfeit. The honesty reset, reciprocal reception and Kikuchi's own initiative matter to what the relationship becomes. At the same time, subsequent affection cannot retroactively remove the origin of access. This supports a developmental argument about chosen relation rather than a purity test about whether a feeling began without mediation. The accepted FK-E01–04/FK-R01–07 register actually supplies the steps used here. The chapter's claim that V07 mutual selection is particular, rather than a general instruction to persist after a refusal, is appropriately limited.

Ordinary life supplies affirmative goods throughout: reading, meals, gifts, a walk, particular bodily closeness, conversation and time spent learning another person's pleasure. They are not merely preparation for a later rescue. The study's account of finite allocation therefore has real stakes. Fumiya cannot solve the V08–V09 problem just by saying that he cares; reducing peripheral activities also cuts actual valued relations and practices. Kikuchi's V09 reselection changes the proposed solution because she answers from her own position. Her answer is neither erased by the protagonist's prior possible-separation decision nor converted into agreement to every later demand on his time. The difference between actual wanted intimacy and exhaustive knowledge is correctly maintained.

The V08.5 comparison is not a decorative supplement. In the freshly reread `text/part0021.html` P80–189, Mimimi says that her love continues and she wants to act honestly without doing wrong; Kikuchi treats the feeling as meaningful. That is not permission for every later act, nor is their private exchange transferred wholesale to Fumiya. Tama returns to the scene and explains that she had waited after seeing its atmosphere; this does not give her the entire preceding dialogue. Later, Tama's account of weight, difficulty and warmth answers a particular friend's fear. The draft uses that reception to explain positive reliance, while leaving future capacity open. It does not make warmth into an obligation to be indefinitely available.

## 2. Recipient, contact and disclosure are treated as separate responsibilities

Mimimi's continuing love is not reduced to an unsuccessful rival's utility. The draft lets that feeling remain real, alongside a self she can choose to like and a refusal to use Fumiya's weakened position opportunistically. This retains her earlier partial self-regard in V09 and avoids making V12 its first appearance. It also avoids predicting perpetual waiting or a replacement exclusive source of worth. Her love, refusal, help and limits are related acts with different objects.

My fresh V09 returns confirm the useful and troublesome sides of her intervention. `text/part0029.html` P137–142 gives her proposed walk, grabbing/pulling, his protest, her continuation and the actual resumed walk. The intervention has an outcome: it restores something he was discarding. Its usefulness does not supply prior consent to the initial contact. The later contact has another sequence: she already leans on him at part0029 P257; part0031 P10 again presents that ongoing contact; P18 asks whether she may remain like this for a little while and P19 gives assent. This is the sole required precision in the submitted body and route row. Later assent concerns continuing contact, not initiating a previously unperformed lean. RC-M01 corrects this without equating the two contacts or importing a general bodily rule.

The Rena comparison is stronger because it keeps an individual person in view. Her social perception, game/community participation and local withdrawals coexist with repeated boundary violations. The manuscript does not erase her ordinary competence to make a warning example. Equally, it does not turn useful affiliation into a claim on Fumiya's body. Spoken refusals, repeated acts, unspoken discomfort, omission from a partner's account and unpermitted phone access retain separate actors and evidentiary status. V11 Rena's appraisal addressed to Kikuchi is not misassigned to Fumiya; arm contact directed at Fumiya remains a different act. Local withdrawal/apology is not broad reform, and the study invents neither a later offense nor a complete rehabilitation.

This distinction also governs absent-party information. A partner's trust does not pool the rights of an absent friend whose private history is discussed. Contributor permission, author's circulation permission, modeled-subject permission and a recipient's willingness to receive a story are not treated as interchangeable. The study can therefore affirm intimacy and collaboration while identifying an unresolved or exceeded scope of authority. That is a concrete literary comparison, not an unsupported legal conclusion.

## 3. Care has costs and sometimes has to refuse

The treatment of Tama, Yuzu, Nakamura and the wider group protects the ensemble from becoming a supply of helpers. Friendship or romantic concern does not establish unlimited labor, readiness or institutional capacity. The V11 replacement/council and later participation sequences retain their own clocks and objects. An actual refusal is not canceled because a person later joins another activity. This is also why neglected event preparation remains consequential: care for one person can displace obligations to other people whose work and expectations remain real.

The family material sustains warmth and injury together. It does not infer a complete motive from an attributed explanation, name an unnamed religion, diagnose a living or dead person, or harmonize the unresolved grade discrepancy. Haruka has sustained initiative and particular private channels, not complete informed authority over all later uses of the information. Nagisa cannot supply posthumous testimony; her intention and the counterfactual prevention question remain open. The study's responsibility argument does not depend on solving those unknowns. The later shared fiction may be received as meaningful without becoming a recovered final answer from her.

The same restraint applies to the V12 island. The manuscript preserves independent local worlds rather than making Mitsu and Andy therapeutic instruments. Mitsu's refusal, maintenance and scoped trusted delegation remain real acts. Fumiya initiates the first costume proposal/opening with Kikuchi's assent; her later trial and Mitsu's expert correction have their own actors. The written blue-color name is correct, while the attached scarlet sample mismatches it. A conjectured swap/knot explanation remains Fumiya's interpretation, not an established culprit or mechanism. Private documents and a loan do not grant blanket prior access, general fictionalization permission or publishing rights. The positive gains are a changed method of attention and collaborative work, with independently inhabited contexts constraining that work.

## 4. V11 and V12 are compared without a false first discovery

The draft does not claim that V12 is the first time Fumiya offers ungrounded reassurance. V11's explicit lack of grounds coexists with the unbeaten credential and command. ## 1. What the argument earns

The central distinction—groups make actions receivable more readily than they establish answerable responsibility—is sustained through different kinds of evidence rather than merely announced. The election tests stored credibility against a manufactured occasion; the harassment sequence tests salience, authorization and victim standing; class production tests differentiated roles; later care tests fit, privacy and burden; the island tests common activity without a compulsory common interpretation. These cases do not all have the same moral outcome. The draft explains why the difference matters instead of placing them in a single successful-control plot.

Its positive claim is substantial. Changed reception can let a person speak, work, object, return or enjoy company. Routine, public form, selected habitats and ordinary coexistence are real goods. The manuscript does not require a perfect institution before these goods count. That prevents its incomplete-justice argument from erasing the actual apologies, useful Konno conduct, Yuzu's chosen work, Takei's ordinary social capacity, the festival's achievement or Hinami's present participation. The account also preserves failure: some capacity is supplied by a harmed person, an absorbing friend, a substitute organizer or a professional, and an output does not settle that distribution.

## 2. Election and captaincy: a changed occasion does not make a transparent field
